No decomposed goal has been dispatched live: the acceptance case is argued from the tick tests against fake-gh, not observed end to end on GitHub.

planTracks marks a running root's nodes `covered` from its status, not from its run record, so a root claimed by hand (or running for any other reason) holds its children for as long as that attempt lives. True before this change for claude-track roots and now true for every inferred one; documented as a known gap on the tracks wiki page. The effect is latency, never a double claim.

Inference makes tracks the common path, so #197's brief-level gaps (a subagent that skips `hkb heartbeat <root>` exposes the whole track to reclaim past stale_after; the verb check is unenforced) now apply to every decomposed goal rather than to the rare adopted one. A root also still needs kb.max_runtime larger than the whole track -- the heartbeat does not defend against max_runtime.

Three files outside the card's declared paths were touched and are disclosed on the PR: src/cli.js (the `hkb track` verb and the `hkb show` line the issue asks for), src/doctor.js (the check the issue asks for) and src/mcp.js (two tokens, so kanban_show keeps returning exactly what `hkb show --json` prints -- a test pins that). results.summary: A root with unfinished children is now dispatched as ONE orchestrated session by default, with no adopt step. The decision is `isTrackRoot(task, cfg, {board})` in src/model.js (pure, four modes): `forced` when the card's own profile has "track": true; `opted-out` on the new `kb:no-track` label; `inferred` when the card has >=1 unfinished child, nothing on the board is still blocked by it, and some track profile's `track_agents` can execute its profile; `none` otherwise. planTracks now asks it which cards are roots instead of reading the agent label, and trackReadiness carries `profile` and `mode` through to the tick. Two things worth knowing for the next worker: (1) the kb:agent:* label is NEVER rewritten -- an inferred root keeps kb:agent:claude and launches on claude-track, because that label is what node dispatch reads on every fallback, so the tick takes the launch profile from cand.profile and counts the running track's slot against that profile's cap via plan.profiles; (2) only the OUTERMOST root is inferred (an interior node of a chain is a node of the bigger track), which is the one part of the decision that needs the whole board, hence the `board` parameter -- `hkb show`, which reads one issue, answers without it. New `hkb track <n> [--off|--on] [--json]` prints the verdict and its reason and toggles kb:no-track; `hkb show` (and kanban_show) repeat it under `track`; `hkb doctor` gains checkTrackProfile, which warns when a board holds cards with unfinished children and no profile with "track": true, and costs no board read when one exists. DEVIATION from the issue, disclosed on the PR: the issue asked for `kb:agent:claude` to be the opt-out, but `hkb create` stamps the default profile on every card, so that is exactly what a freshly decomposed root already wears -- using it would mean nothing is ever inferred. The opt-out is the explicit `kb:no-track` label instead; forcing is unchanged, and a forced profile beats kb:no-track.

The init half is covered by test/init.test.js.
